summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted after undergoing radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for a liver tumor. He presented with post-procedural hypotension and lethargy, initially attributed to pain medications. During his hospitalization, he developed a right hemothorax, which was managed with chest tube drainage. He also experienced intermittent fevers, but cultures from blood, urine, and ascitic fluid showed no infection, suggesting a post-procedural inflammatory cause. His condition improved with supportive care, including fluid management, pain control, and diuretics for ascites. The chest tube was removed without recurrence, and he was transitioned to oral medications. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for chemo-embolization of a second liver lesion and close outpatient follow-up.
